overview.description: A hybrid parliament-swarm consensus trading system where six specialized AI agents independently analyze prediction market opportunities on Kalshi through isolated information contexts, then vote on whether to execute each trade — with a multi-model swarm layer providing cross-architecture validation on high-value opportunities. Kalshi is a CFTC-regulated Designated Contract Market offering YES/NO event contracts across crypto prices, economics (CPI, Fed rate, GDP), politics, climate/weather, company earnings, and sports outcomes — all cash-settled in USD with a central limit order book. The architecture leverages Claude Code's native infrastructure — MCP servers for live Kalshi API data, CLAUDE.md for immutable trading rules, the skill system for typed capabilities with progressive context loading, subagent orchestration for parallel execution, and hooks for event-driven monitoring and alerts. Each agent specializes in a distinct analytical domain (geopolitics, economics, science, sports, crypto, climate/weather), receives domain-specific data feeds, and produces a structured vote with confidence score and reasoning. A consensus threshold of 4/6 agents must agree before execution. v3.0 adds three architectural tiers from the knowledge overview: (1) Parliament tier — domain-expert agents with dissent reports and minority value tracking, where the Science Agent's empirical role as the most valuable minority dissenter is systematically exploited; (2) Swarm tier — optional multi-model consensus (Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Llama) as a corrective second layer on high-value trades, querying the same question across different model architectures to eliminate single-provider bias; (3) Skill tier — functional decomposition of trading capabilities (EV calculation, Bayesian probability updates, capped Kelly sizing, log-return tracking) as modular skills with progressive context loading that activates deep computation only when basic checks pass. An Exchange Manager abstraction layer decouples all trading logic from Kalshi-specific API details, enabling future platform additions without changing agent logic. The RBI framework (Research, Backtest, Implement) gates all strategies through historical validation before live deployment. All Kalshi prices are in CENTS (0-10000 range). A confidence calibration framework addresses the previously unresolved gap of comparing confidence scores across agents with different domain characteristics. Four open-source reference implementations (Paperclip, MiroFish, Hermes, OpenClaw) inform the implementation, with OpenClaw providing the closest Claude Code integration pattern and Hermes providing the best parliament-style voting reference.
objectives: Outperform single-agent trading by 20%+ ROI through ensemble consensus filtering across parliament and optional swarm layers
Eliminate single-model overconfidence by requiring adversarial validation across 6 specialized agents with dissent reports on split votes
Reduce average loss size by 50% through consensus gating — refuse entry when agents cannot agree
Increase win rate from ~60% (single-agent baseline) to 74%+ through multi-perspective analysis
Surface high-value dissent signals — track and exploit the Science Agent's empirical pattern as most valuable minority dissenter (validate over 30+ solo-dissent events)
Enable fully autonomous 24/7 execution with no human intervention required for standard trades
Implement Kelly Criterion position sizing derived from per-agent confidence scores, historical performance, and confidence calibration weights
Exploit Kalshi's broad market categories — crypto price contracts, economics (CPI, Fed rate, GDP), politics, sports, climate/weather, company earnings — through dedicated specialist agents
Detect within-platform arbitrage on paired YES/NO contracts where prices deviate from 100 cents after fees
Provide progressive signal loading so agents can be added/removed without rebuilding the system — skills activate in tiers (basic checks first, deep computation only when warranted)
Maintain full audit trail of all votes, dissent reports, and execution decisions for iterative improvement and RBI backtesting
Operate within full CFTC regulatory compliance on a regulated Designated Contract Market
Implement multi-model swarm validation as an optional second consensus layer for high-value trades, querying Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Llama in parallel
Decouple trading logic from platform specifics via Exchange Manager pattern — enabling future platform additions without agent changes
Implement confidence calibration framework to normalize agent confidence scores across domains and detect systematically over- or under-confident agents
Gate all strategies through the RBI framework: Research ideas, Backtest against Kalshi historical data, Implement only strategies with proven statistical edge
constraints: Each agent MUST operate in an isolated information context — shared information collapses diversity and defeats the purpose. Claude Code implementation: each subagent gets a different system prompt and tool permission set scoping its data access
Minimum consensus threshold of 4/6 agents required for any trade execution at the parliament tier
Maximum risk per position governed by CLAUDE.md rules — no agent can override the risk ceiling
All agents must return structured output: direction (YES/NO/ABSTAIN), confidence (0-100), reasoning (text), sources (array), and calibrated_confidence (0-100, post-calibration)
Dissent reports are mandatory when the parliament splits — minority agents must produce counterarguments with specific sources
Kelly Criterion sizing with a fractional cap (half-Kelly or quarter-Kelly) to prevent catastrophic drawdown
System must handle API rate limits, network failures, and agent timeouts gracefully with fallback to NO_TRADE

Latency budget: full parliament vote cycle targets p50=60s, p95=120s. The 30-second per-agent timeout will produce frequent ABSTAINs on complex markets; to mitigate, Market Scanner must pre-fetch and cache all domain-specific data feeds at scan time so agents receive pre-loaded data packages rather than fetching live during their analysis window. Agents should spend their 30 seconds on analysis, not data retrieval.
No agent may access another agent's raw analysis — only the orchestrator sees all votes
Human override capability must exist for emergency halt, but standard operation is fully autonomous
All trading must comply with Kalshi's per-market position limits (varies by contract, often $25K-$100K notional) and platform terms of service
Settlement is in USD — no cryptocurrency, no wallet management, no gas fees

Multi-model swarm tier is optional and additive — the parliament must function independently without the swarm layer. Swarm adds latency and cost; trigger only for positions above configurable threshold (default: 3% of bankroll)
Exchange Manager must enforce Kalshi-only execution for US-based trading to maintain CFTC compliance — platform routing to non-CFTC venues is a future capability gated by jurisdictional rules
RBI backtesting must complete on Kalshi historical contract resolution data before any strategy is deployed live — no strategy goes live without passing backtest validation

components.name: Orchestrator (Parliament Speaker)
components.description: The central coordination layer that manages the full trade evaluation lifecycle across both parliament and optional swarm tiers. Receives candidate markets from the Market Scanner, distributes them to all 6 specialist agents in parallel, collects structured votes, applies consensus logic, triggers dissent report generation when splits occur, optionally escalates high-value trades to the multi-model swarm tier, computes aggregate confidence with calibration adjustments, determines Kelly-sized position, and dispatches execution orders via the Exchange Manager. Implements the harness architecture pattern from claw-code: runtime context scoping with typed I/O contracts and scoped agent permissions. The orchestrator never makes trading decisions itself — it is purely a coordination and aggregation layer. In v3.0, the Orchestrator also manages the Model Registry for swarm dispatch and feeds calibration data from the Confidence Calibration Engine into position sizing.

Fan out market data to all 6 specialist agents in parallel via subagent dispatch
Collect structured vote responses with timeout handling (30s per agent, fallback to ABSTAIN)
Apply consensus threshold logic: 4/6 minimum agreement for execution
Trigger mandatory dissent report generation on split votes (4:2, 5:1, etc.)
Compute weighted aggregate confidence from individual agent scores, adjusted by Confidence Calibration Engine weights
Calculate Kelly-sized position based on calibrated aggregate probability estimate and current bankroll
For high-value positions (above swarm_threshold from CLAUDE.md), escalate to Multi-Model Swarm for cross-architecture validation before execution
Dispatch execution orders to the Exchange Manager (not directly to Kalshi)
Log all votes, reasoning, dissent reports, swarm validation results, and decisions to the Audit Trail
Implement circuit breakers: halt trading if daily loss limit reached or if win rate drops below threshold over rolling window
Manage Model Registry for swarm agent dispatch — verify model availability before each swarm session

components.name: Market Scanner
components.description: Continuously monitors Kalshi for tradeable opportunities using progressive context loading — basic checks (liquidity, spread, contract availability) run first as Tier 1 skills; deep computations (probability updates, portfolio impact, cross-agent confirmation) trigger only when Tier 1 passes. Scans all active events and markets at configurable intervals (default: every 15 minutes) using Kalshi's category/tag-filtered event listings (GET /events with status, series_ticker, with_nested_markets filters) and category discovery (GET /search/tags_by_categories). Uses batch orderbook endpoint (GET /markets/orderbooks, up to 100 tickers) for efficient multi-market scanning. Filters by liquidity minimums, volume thresholds, and time-to-resolution. Identifies within-platform arbitrage opportunities where paired YES/NO contracts deviate from 100 cents after fees. Routes candidate markets to the appropriate specialist agent(s) based on Kalshi's structured category-to-tag mappings. Outputs a ranked list of CandidateMarket objects to the Orchestrator. Inspired by the PHANTOM system's approach of tracking thousands of markets simultaneously. v3.0: Implements the progressive context loading pattern — 147+ contracts scanned per session on average, resulting in only 2-3 entries per day that pass all tiers.

Use GET /search/tags_by_categories for structured category->tag discovery to map markets to agent specializations

Pass CandidateMarket objects to Orchestrator with full market metadata as JSON

components.name: Science & Technology Agent
components.description: Analyzes markets through a scientific and technological lens. Receives research publications, clinical trial data, patent filings, regulatory submissions (FDA, EMA), and technology adoption curves. Specializes in scientific breakthroughs, drug approvals, technology milestones, climate events, and company earnings tied to tech sector fundamentals. The most contrarian agent in historical testing — voted against the majority on 40% of markets, and when it was the sole dissenter against the majority, it was correct 80% of the time (4 out of 5 events). NOTE: The 80% figure is from a 5-sample pilot and cannot be treated as statistically reliable. This metric must be re-evaluated after 30+ solo-dissent events are observed before being used to drive automated decisions. v3.0 designates this agent as the 'most valuable minority dissenter' based on the knowledge overview's finding that a single dissenting agent proved more valuable than the rest of the system combined on its minority calls — the Dissent Analyzer gives this agent's dissent reports elevated scrutiny and the Confidence Calibration Engine tracks whether its contrarian tendency is genuinely predictive or a prompt artifact.

components.name: Exchange Manager
components.description: v3.0 addition: A routing abstraction layer that decouples all trading logic from Kalshi-specific API implementations. All components (Market Scanner, Execution Engine, Portfolio Tracker) interact with Kalshi exclusively through this manager — never calling Kalshi API endpoints directly. This enables: (1) a single line of configuration to switch between Kalshi production and demo APIs, (2) future addition of new exchanges without changing agent logic, (3) enforcement of jurisdictional routing rules (US-based = Kalshi only for CFTC compliance), (4) unified handling of contract identifiers, order formats, and settlement mechanics across potential future platforms. Currently configured with Kalshi as the sole adapter. Inspired by the exchange manager pattern from the multi-model swarm architecture where the same agent system operates across multiple platforms with zero code changes in agents.

components.description: Handles all trade execution after the Parliament (and optionally the Swarm) approves a position. Communicates with Kalshi exclusively through the Exchange Manager. Manages order placement, order amendment, batch operations, slippage control, partial fill handling, and position tracking. All prices and balances are in CENTS. Sends Telegram alerts on fills, drawdown warnings, and daily P&L summaries. All settlement is in USD — no wallet management, no gas fees, no on-chain transactions. Can leverage subaccounts (up to 32) for per-agent trade isolation.
responsibilities: Receive ExecutionOrder from Orchestrator with approved position size and direction
Place orders via Exchange Manager (POST /portfolio/orders with ticker, side, count, price, order type)
Implement slippage protection: reject execution if best available price has moved more than 2% from analysis time
Handle partial fills gracefully — re-queue remainder or cancel based on time sensitivity
Track all open positions with real-time P&L via Exchange Manager positions endpoint
Monitor fills via WebSocket stream (through Exchange Manager) for immediate execution confirmation
Execute paired contract arbitrage at maximum speed when Sports Agent detects mispricing
Send Telegram alerts on: order fills, position closures, drawdown threshold crossings, daily P&L summary
Implement emergency halt: cease all trading and cancel open orders if daily loss exceeds CLAUDE.md limit

GRACEFUL SHUTDOWN: On system halt (manual, circuit breaker, or crash recovery): (1) Cancel all pending/open orders immediately via Exchange Manager, (2) Log all open position states to persistent storage (SQLite) with current market prices, (3) Do NOT auto-close positions on shutdown — positions on prediction markets cannot be 'closed' without selling at current market price which may realize unnecessary losses, (4) On restart, validate persisted state against live positions via Exchange Manager before resuming trading, (5) Send Telegram alert with shutdown reason and open position summary, (6) Require explicit human confirmation before resuming autonomous trading after an unclean shutdown
interfaces: Input: ExecutionOrder {ticker, event_ticker, direction: 'yes'|'no', count, limit_price_cents, order_type: 'limit'|'market', urgency, subaccount_id?: string}
Output: ExecutionResult {order_id, fill_price_cents, fill_count, status, timestamp, fees_cents}
Output: TelegramAlert via webhook
Output: PositionUpdate to Portfolio Tracker
Dependency: Exchange Manager (all Kalshi API calls go through Exchange Manager)

components.name: Portfolio Tracker & Risk Manager
components.description: Maintains real-time portfolio state, enforces risk limits, and tracks performance metrics against benchmarks. Computes rolling win rate, average win/loss ratio, Sharpe ratio equivalent, and maximum drawdown. Inspired by the $50K Claude Portfolio concept of live, transparent performance tracking. Enforces all CLAUDE.md risk rules as hard constraints that no agent or orchestrator can override. Also enforces Kalshi's per-market position limits by querying market rules through the Exchange Manager before approving orders.
responsibilities: Maintain real-time portfolio state: all open positions, USD cash balance, total equity
Enforce maximum position size (from CLAUDE.md rules) — reject orders that exceed per-trade or total exposure limits
Enforce Kalshi's per-market position limits (varies by contract) — query market rules via Exchange Manager and reject orders exceeding platform limits
Track rolling performance metrics: win rate, avg win/loss, total ROI, max drawdown, Sharpe-equivalent, log-return tracking
Compare performance against single-agent baseline to measure parliament alpha
Implement drawdown circuit breaker: pause trading if drawdown exceeds configurable threshold (e.g., 15% of bankroll)
Generate daily performance report with per-agent accuracy breakdown
Track which agent's dissent was correct retroactively — update agent credibility scores over time
Track settlement fees per contract to ensure edge calculations account for Kalshi's fee structure (typically 1-7 cents per contract on settlement)

EXIT MANAGER: Monitor open positions for early exit conditions — cut losses when position moves against by configurable threshold (default: 15% of position value), take profit when position reaches configurable target (default: 2x edge captured), and trigger re-evaluation when material new information arrives (breaking news, data feed alert, or agent-initiated signal)

EXIT MANAGER: Maintain per-position exit rules at entry time: stop-loss price, take-profit price, and re-evaluation triggers. Dispatch a reduced parliament session (4 agents, 15-second timeout) for re-evaluation votes on whether to hold, exit, or adjust size
EXIT MANAGER: Execute early exits via Execution Engine (through Exchange Manager) with same slippage protections as entry orders. Log exit rationale to Audit Trail with entry-vs-exit P&L attribution
interfaces: Input: PositionUpdate from Execution Engine
Input: MarketSettlement events from Exchange Manager (market resolution and payout data)
Input: ExitTrigger {position_id, trigger_type: 'stop_loss'|'take_profit'|'re_evaluation'|'manual', trigger_data}
Output: PortfolioState {equity_cents, cash_cents, positions[], metrics{}}
Output: RiskVeto — can block ExecutionOrders that violate risk limits or Kalshi position limits
Output: ExitOrder {position_id, direction, count, reason, exit_type} to Execution Engine
Output: PerformanceReport (daily/weekly)

components.name: Dissent Analyzer
components.description: A meta-analytical component that specifically processes and weights dissent signals. When the parliament splits, this component analyzes the minority dissent reports, cross-references them with historical outcomes, and assigns a 'dissent quality score' that can modify the Orchestrator's final decision. Based on the empirical finding that the Science Agent's solo dissent against the majority was correct 4 out of 5 times — saving $890 in avoided losses from a single agent's contrarian signal. v3.0 formalizes the knowledge overview's key finding: 'A single dissenting agent proved more valuable than the rest of the system combined on its minority calls.' The Dissent Analyzer turns this pattern from anecdote into systematic edge. It also creates an audit trail of dissent reports for post-hoc analysis of decision quality — critical for the RBI framework's research phase.
responsibilities: Receive all dissent reports from minority-voting agents

Score dissent quality based on: specificity of sources cited, historical accuracy of the dissenting agent on similar markets, strength of counterargument, and Kalshi-specific regulatory or structural risk flags
Maintain per-agent dissent accuracy tracking: when agent X dissents, how often is X ultimately correct?

Flag 'high-quality dissent' scenarios: e.g., Science Agent sole dissenter with >80 confidence = historically 80% accurate (5-sample pilot — do not trust accuracy score for automated escalation decisions until minimum 30 solo-dissent events per agent have been recorded; until then, always escalate to HUMAN_REVIEW rather than auto-ABORT or auto-PROCEED)
Can escalate dissent to human review or reduce position size when dissent quality score exceeds threshold
Feed dissent accuracy data back to Orchestrator for dynamic confidence weighting
Feed dissent patterns to the RBI Backtest Engine for correlation analysis with market outcomes
interfaces: Input: DissentReport {agent_name, vote, confidence, reasoning, sources, market_context, kalshi_regulatory_flags?: string[]}
Output: DissentScore {quality: 0-100, historical_accuracy: float, recommendation: PROCEED|REDUCE_SIZE|HUMAN_REVIEW|ABORT}
Output: AgentCredibilityUpdate to Orchestrator and Confidence Calibration Engine

components.name: Multi-Model Swarm Validator
components.description: v3.0 addition: An optional second consensus layer that queries the same trading question across multiple AI model providers (Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, Llama) in parallel. Triggered only for high-value positions (above swarm_threshold in CLAUDE.md, default: 3% of bankroll). The swarm does not replace the parliament — it ratifies or refuses parliament-approved trades based on cross-architecture model agreement. Different model architectures have different failure modes: if 5 different model families agree, confidence is higher than any single model alone. If models disagree, it signals regime uncertainty that the parliament's same-model agents cannot detect. Acts as a corrective second layer on the parliament's decision, not a replacement. A consensus reviewer aggregates all model responses into a final SwarmResult.
responsibilities: Receive parliament-approved trade with full context (votes, dissent reports, market data, aggregate confidence) from Orchestrator
Query the same trading question to agents running on Claude, GPT-4, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Llama (5 model providers minimum)
Run all model queries in parallel with 45-second timeout per model (longer than parliament agents due to cross-provider latency)
Collect structured responses from all models: direction, confidence, reasoning
Apply consensus reviewer logic: compute cross-model agreement rate and model-diversity-weighted confidence
Return SwarmResult with ratify/refuse/reduce recommendation to Orchestrator
Track per-model accuracy over time to weight reliable models higher in consensus calculation
Detect single-provider bias: flag when all Claude-family models agree but non-Claude models disagree (or vice versa)
Can weight models differently based on domain performance (e.g., Claude for reasoning-heavy political markets, GPT for data-dense sports markets) — learned from historical accuracy data
interfaces: Input: SwarmRequest {parliament_decision: ParliamentDecision, market_data: CandidateMarket, full_context: object}
Output: SwarmResult {recommendation: 'ratify'|'refuse'|'reduce_size', cross_model_agreement: float, model_votes: ModelVote[], confidence_adjustment: float}
Dependency: Model Registry for provider connections and health checks

components.name: Model Registry
components.description: v3.0 addition: A centralized registry for AI models that enables easy swapping and updating as new models release. Supports multiple providers: Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT), Google (Gemini), DeepSeek, Meta (Llama). Includes a testing framework that verifies each model with a simple prompt to confirm operational status before use. Decouples agent logic from specific model versions, ensuring the system always uses the most capable available models. Critical for the Multi-Model Swarm Validator — need reliable connections to 5+ model providers simultaneously.
responsibilities: Maintain registry of available models with provider, version, API endpoint, and capability tags
Verify model availability before each swarm session with a simple test prompt
Handle model version updates: when a provider releases a new version, update registry and re-run verification
Provide model selection API: given domain and task type, return the best available model(s)
Track per-model latency, availability, and cost for optimization
Support fallback chains: if primary model for a provider is unavailable, use backup model
Enforce cost budgets: track API spend per model per day and halt swarm queries if budget exceeded
interfaces: Input: ModelQuery {provider?: string, domain?: string, task_type?: string}
Output: ModelSelection {model_id, provider, version, endpoint, estimated_latency_ms, cost_per_query}
Output: ModelHealthReport {model_id, status: 'available'|'degraded'|'unavailable', last_verified}

components.name: Confidence Calibration Engine
components.description: v3.0 addition: Addresses the previously identified knowledge gap of confidence calibration across agents. Each parliament agent returns a confidence score (0-100), but these scores are not inherently comparable across domains — a Crypto Agent's '80% confidence' may have very different reliability than a Science Agent's '80% confidence'. The Calibration Engine maintains per-agent, per-domain calibration curves that map raw confidence scores to calibrated probabilities based on historical accuracy. This ensures that when the Orchestrator computes aggregate confidence for Kelly sizing, the input probabilities are meaningfully comparable. Also detects and corrects for systematically over- or under-confident agents.
responsibilities: Maintain per-agent calibration curves: for each agent, track historical accuracy at each confidence level (e.g., when Crypto Agent says 80%, how often is it correct?)
Apply calibration adjustment to raw confidence scores before they enter aggregate confidence computation
Detect systematic bias: flag agents that are consistently overconfident (claimed 80%, actual 55%) or underconfident (claimed 60%, actual 78%)
Generate calibration reports per agent per Kalshi category for the weekly learning cycle
Feed calibrated probabilities to Kelly Sizer for more accurate position sizing
Bootstrap calibration with uninformative priors (assume perfect calibration) during the cold-start phase, switching to empirical calibration after minimum 50 settled votes per agent
Implement Platt scaling or isotonic regression for calibration curve fitting
Track cross-model calibration for swarm agents: different model providers have different confidence distributions
interfaces: Input: RawVote {agent_name, domain, raw_confidence: 0-100, direction}
Input: OutcomeData {agent_name, domain, predicted_confidence, actual_outcome}
Output: CalibratedVote {agent_name, raw_confidence, calibrated_confidence, calibration_method, sample_size}
Output: CalibrationReport {agent_name, domain, brier_score, calibration_curve_points[], bias_direction: 'over'|'under'|'well_calibrated', sample_count}

components.name: RBI Backtest Engine
components.description: v3.0 addition: Implements the Research-Backtest-Implement framework that gates all strategies through historical validation before live deployment. Uses Kalshi's historical contract resolution data (GET /historical/markets, GET /historical/trades) to backtest agent strategies against actual CFTC-regulated outcomes. This is the gatekeeper that prevents untested strategies from reaching live capital. Inspired by Jim Simons' approach at Renaissance Technologies: if an idea worked historically, it is more likely to work in the future (with caveats on regime changes and sample size).
responsibilities: RESEARCH: Maintain a continuously updated list of trading strategy hypotheses from agent performance analysis, dissent pattern mining, and market regime observations
BACKTEST: Test each strategy hypothesis against Kalshi historical data — simulate parliament votes, Kelly sizing, and execution on past markets to compute theoretical P&L
IMPLEMENT: Promote only strategies that show positive expected value in backtest with statistically significant sample size (minimum 100 simulated trades, positive Sharpe)
Prevent deployment of any strategy that has not passed backtesting — this is a hard gate, not a recommendation
Support walk-forward validation: train on historical period A, validate on subsequent unseen period B
Track regime sensitivity: flag strategies that worked in one market regime (e.g., low volatility) but may fail in another
Provide confidence intervals on backtest results — point estimates without uncertainty bounds are misleading
Feed backtest results to the Orchestrator's learning loop for strategy weight adjustment
interfaces: Input: StrategyHypothesis {name, description, entry_rules, exit_rules, sizing_rules, target_categories}
Input: HistoricalData from Exchange Manager (GET /historical/markets, GET /historical/trades)

Output: BacktestResult {strategy_name, simulated_trades: number, win_rate, total_pnl_cents, sharpe, max_drawdown, confidence_interval_95, regime_sensitivity: object, recommendation: 'promote'|'reject'|'needs_more_data'}
Output: PromotedStrategy to Orchestrator for live deployment

components.name: Audit Trail & Learning System
components.description: Persistent storage and analysis of all parliament decisions, swarm validations, agent votes, market outcomes, and performance attribution. Enables retroactive analysis of which agents were right, which dissent signals had value, how swarm validation affected outcomes, and how consensus quality correlates with results. This is the learning loop that allows the system to improve over time by adjusting agent credibility weights, calibration curves, and consensus thresholds based on empirical results.
responsibilities: Log every parliament session: market analyzed, all 6 votes with reasoning, consensus outcome, swarm validation result (if triggered), execution decision, final P&L
Track market settlements on Kalshi (via Exchange Manager) and attribute outcomes to individual agent accuracy
Compute rolling accuracy by agent, by market category (using Kalshi's category taxonomy), and by consensus split pattern
Identify systematic biases: is any agent consistently overconfident? Consistently wrong on a market type?
Generate weekly learning reports recommending adjustments to agent weights, calibration curves, or data feeds
Store all data in SQLite with structured schemas for downstream analysis and model fine-tuning
Feed historical outcome data to Confidence Calibration Engine for calibration curve updates
Feed dissent outcome data to Dissent Analyzer for dissent accuracy tracking
Feed strategy performance data to RBI Backtest Engine for hypothesis generation
interfaces: Input: ParliamentSession {market, votes[], decision, swarm_result?, execution, outcome}
Output: SQLite audit records (append-only, structured schemas)
Output: WeeklyLearningReport with recommendations
Output: AgentAccuracyMetrics for dynamic weight adjustment
Output: CalibrationData to Confidence Calibration Engine
Output: StrategyPerformanceData to RBI Backtest Engine

architecture.data_flow: 1. MARKET DISCOVERY (Tier 1 — Progressive Loading): Market Scanner polls Kalshi events API via Exchange Manager (GET /events with status/series_ticker filters) and uses GET /search/tags_by_categories for structured category->tag discovery. Retrieves batch orderbooks (GET /markets/orderbooks, up to 100 tickers) for efficient multi-market scanning. Applies Tier 1 basic checks: liquidity minimums, spread validation, time-to-resolution, contract availability. Rejects the majority of 147+ scanned contracts at this stage with minimal computation. 2. EDGE ESTIMATION (Tier 2 — Progressive Loading): Markets passing Tier 1 undergo Tier 2 analysis: the market-analyzer skill computes implied probability, compares P(real) from external forecasts against P(market) from current contract prices, and requires a minimum spread of 0.07. Only markets with estimated positive EV after settlement fees advance. Each candidate is tagged with Kalshi's category/tag mappings for agent routing. Pre-fetches domain-specific data feeds for all agents that will receive this candidate. 3. PROGRESSIVE SIGNAL LOADING: For each CandidateMarket passing Tier 2, the Orchestrator prepares 6 isolated data packages — each containing the base market JSON (ticker, title, yes_price_cents, no_price_cents, deadline, volume_cents, category, tags) plus domain-specific feeds unique to that agent. Geopolitics gets diplomatic briefings; Economics gets Fed minutes, CPI data, and yield curves; Science gets clinical trials and research; Sports gets stats, injury reports, AND Kalshi live game data via Exchange Manager; Crypto gets exchange flows and CEX price feeds; Climate/Weather gets NOAA forecasts and station data. No agent sees another agent's data. 4. PARALLEL AGENT DISPATCH: Orchestrator dispatches all 6 specialist agents simultaneously as Claude Code subagents. Each runs in its own context with its own system prompt. 30-second timeout per agent; timeout = ABSTAIN vote. 5. VOTE COLLECTION & CALIBRATION: Each agent returns structured JSON: {direction, confidence, reasoning, sources, domain_signals}. Confidence Calibration Engine adjusts raw confidence scores to calibrated probabilities based on per-agent historical accuracy. Orchestrator collects all 6 calibrated votes. 6. CONSENSUS EVALUATION: Orchestrator applies threshold: 4/6 minimum agreement on direction. If threshold not met, NO_TRADE and log the disagreement. 7. DISSENT PROCESSING: On split votes (4:2 or 5:1), minority agents produce dissent reports. Dissent Analyzer scores quality, checks historical accuracy of the dissenting agent(s), and flags Kalshi-specific regulatory/structural risks. High-quality dissent can reduce position size or escalate to human review. 8. OPTIONAL SWARM VALIDATION: For positions above swarm_threshold (default: 3% of bankroll), Orchestrator escalates to Multi-Model Swarm Validator. The same question is sent to Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Llama in parallel. Swarm consensus reviewer aggregates cross-model responses and returns ratify/refuse/reduce recommendation. Swarm refusal = NO_TRADE regardless of parliament consensus. Swarm reduce = position size cut by 50%. 9. POSITION SIZING: If consensus reached (and swarm ratified, if triggered), Orchestrator computes Kelly-sized position using calibrated aggregate probability estimate against market odds (in cents), capped at half-Kelly. Portfolio Tracker validates against CLAUDE.md risk limits and Kalshi's per-market position limits (queried via Exchange Manager). 10. EXECUTION: Execution Engine places order via Exchange Manager. Slippage check against orderbook, fill confirmation via WebSocket, Telegram alert. Can use subaccounts for per-agent trade isolation. 11. SETTLEMENT TRACKING: When market settles on Kalshi, Audit Trail records outcome and payout (in cents), attributes accuracy to each agent and swarm models, updates credibility scores. Calibration Engine receives outcome data for calibration curve updates. 12. LEARNING LOOP: Weekly, the system reviews agent accuracy by domain and Kalshi category/tag mappings (from GET /search/tags_by_categories), adjusts credibility weights, updates calibration curves, and flags agents that need data feed improvements. RBI Backtest Engine receives strategy performance data for hypothesis generation and validation.

integration_points.name: Kalshi MCP Server (via Exchange Manager)
integration_points.description: Primary MCP server wrapping Kalshi's REST API (https://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/v2). All access goes through the Exchange Manager abstraction layer. Authenticates via RSA-PSS key-pair signing on every request (stateless, no login endpoint, no token refresh). Provides event listings with category/tag filtering, market data, orderbook snapshots (single and batch), order management (including batch and amend), position tracking, fill history, live game data for sports, milestones, historical archives, and category/tag discovery. Also maintains a WebSocket connection (wss://api.elections.kalshi.com/trade-api/ws/v2) for real-time orderbook and fill streaming. This is the sole prediction market integration — all trading executes through Kalshi.

authentication.flow: Load PEM private key from KALSHI_PRIVATE_KEY_PATH. For each request, construct the signing message as '{timestamp_ms}{HTTP_METHOD}{path_without_query_params}' (e.g., '1716000000000GET/trade-api/v2/portfolio/positions'). Sign with RSA-PSS using SHA-256 digest, MGF1-SHA256 mask generation, and salt length equal to digest length. Include three headers on every request: KALSHI-ACCESS-KEY (the API key ID), KALSHI-ACCESS-TIMESTAMP (the timestamp_ms string), and KALSHI-ACCESS-SIGNATURE (the base64-encoded signature). Requires the 'cryptography' Python package for RSA-PSS operations.
authentication.stateless: No JWT tokens, no login endpoint, no token refresh needed. Each request is independently authenticated via its signature headers.
authentication.sdk: kalshi_python_sync / kalshi_python_async (NOT 'kalshi-python'). The SDK handles RSA-PSS signing internally when configured with the API key ID and private key path.
authentication.demo_api: https://demo-api.kalshi.co/trade-api/v2 for paper trading (same RSA-PSS auth, separate API key pair)

Historical endpoints (GET /historical/markets, GET /historical/trades) are critical for the RBI Backtest Engine — provide the dataset for strategy validation.

skill_definitions.description: Calculates implied probability, edge, and expected value for a given Kalshi event contract. Used by Market Scanner (Tier 2 progressive loading) and individual agents. Compares P(real) from external forecasts against P(market) from current contract prices. Implements the core EV calculation from the skill architecture pattern.
skill_definitions.inputs: MarketData {ticker, yes_price_cents, no_price_cents, volume_cents, open_interest, close_time, category, tags}
skill_definitions.outputs: MarketAnalysis {implied_prob, p_real_estimate, edge_vs_fair, expected_value_cents, liquidity_grade, time_to_resolution, settlement_fee_impact_cents, p_real_minus_p_market_spread, recommendation}
skill_definitions.invocation: Claude Code skill invoked via /market-analyzer or programmatically by Orchestrator. Progressive loading: Tier 1 checks (liquidity, spread) run first; this skill fires only at Tier 2.

skill_definitions.description: Computes optimal position size using Kelly Criterion given calibrated probability estimate, market odds, and current bankroll. Applies fractional Kelly cap. Accounts for Kalshi's settlement fees in edge calculation. v3.0: Accepts calibrated probability from Confidence Calibration Engine rather than raw agent confidence.
skill_definitions.inputs: KellyInput {calibrated_prob, market_price_cents, bankroll_cents, kelly_fraction: 0.25|0.5|1.0, max_position_pct, settlement_fee_cents, consensus_split: '6:0'|'5:1'|'4:2'}
skill_definitions.outputs: KellyOutput {optimal_count, optimal_size_cents, kelly_fraction_used, edge_after_fees, expected_growth_rate, split_adjustment_applied: boolean}
skill_definitions.formula: f* = (p * b - q) / b, where p = calibrated probability (from Confidence Calibration Engine), q = 1-p, b = net odds adjusted for settlement fees. All Kalshi prices are in CENTS (0-10000 range). For Kalshi YES contracts priced at p_market_cents, payout is 100 cents minus settlement fee. Example: if calibrated probability p=0.70, market price p_market=55 cents, and settlement fee is 3 cents, then net payout = 100 - 3 = 97 cents, profit per contract if correct = 97 - 55 = 42 cents, b = 42 / 55 = 0.764, and f* = (0.70 * 0.764 - 0.30) / 0.764 = (0.535 - 0.30) / 0.764 = 0.307, meaning Kelly-optimal is 30.7% of bankroll (before fractional cap). At half-Kelly, position size = 15.35% of bankroll, further capped by max_position_pct and Kalshi's per-market position limit. On split consensus (4:2), automatic 25% size reduction per RISK-006.

skill_definitions.description: v3.0 addition: Continuously refines probability estimates by comparing P(real) from external forecasts against P(market) from current contract prices using Bayesian updating. Pulls live contract data every 15 minutes and updates posterior probability. The spread between P(real) and P(market) defines the trading edge. From the skill architecture pattern that achieved 79% win rate.
skill_definitions.inputs: BayesianInput {prior_prob, new_evidence: {source, direction, strength}, market_price_cents, last_update_timestamp}
skill_definitions.outputs: BayesianOutput {posterior_prob, p_real, p_market, spread, update_magnitude, evidence_chain: {source, impact}[]}

skill_definitions.description: Generates a structured dissent report when an agent is in the minority on a split vote. Forces the agent to produce specific counterarguments with source citations. v3.0: Includes Kalshi-specific regulatory/structural risk flags in dissent output.
skill_definitions.inputs: DissentInput {agent_name, agent_vote, majority_direction, market_data, agent_reasoning, agent_sources}
skill_definitions.outputs: DissentReport {counterarguments: string[], risk_factors: string[], kalshi_regulatory_flags: string[], sources: string[], confidence_in_dissent: 0-100, recommended_action: 'proceed'|'reduce_size'|'abort'}

skill_definitions.description: Orchestrates a complete parliament voting session for a single market. Dispatches all 6 agents in parallel, collects votes, applies calibration adjustments, processes consensus logic, processes dissent, optionally triggers swarm validation, computes position size, and returns a final decision.
skill_definitions.inputs: SessionInput {candidate_market: CandidateMarket, bankroll_cents: number, risk_limits: RiskLimits, swarm_threshold_pct: number}
skill_definitions.outputs: SessionOutput {decision: 'EXECUTE'|'NO_TRADE'|'HUMAN_REVIEW', votes: Vote[], calibrated_votes: CalibratedVote[], dissent_reports: DissentReport[], swarm_result?: SwarmResult, position_size_cents: number, contract_count: number, aggregate_confidence: number, calibrated_aggregate_confidence: number, execution_order?: ExecutionOrder}

skill_definitions.description: Detects arbitrage opportunities in paired YES/NO contracts on Kalshi where prices deviate from 100 cents after settlement fees. All prices in cents. Operates through Exchange Manager.

v3.0 addition: Dispatches a parliament-approved trade to multiple AI model providers for cross-architecture validation. Uses the Model Registry to select and query models, then applies consensus reviewer logic to produce a ratify/refuse/reduce recommendation.

claude_md_rules.description: Immutable trading rules enforced via CLAUDE.md. These are loaded into every agent's context at runtime and cannot be overridden by any agent or the orchestrator. They represent hard risk management constraints.

rules.name: Maximum Position Size
rules.rule: Never risk more than 5% of total bankroll on a single position. This applies regardless of confidence score or consensus strength. Additionally, respect Kalshi's per-market position limits (varies by contract, often $25K-$100K notional) — the more restrictive of CLAUDE.md or Kalshi's limit applies.
rules.enforcement: Portfolio Tracker validates against both CLAUDE.md limits and Kalshi per-market limits (via Exchange Manager) before execution; Execution Engine rejects oversized orders

rules.name: Minimum Edge Threshold
rules.rule: Do not enter any position where estimated edge AFTER settlement fees is less than 7% (difference between calibrated probability and implied market probability, minus settlement fee impact). Below this threshold, fees and model uncertainty consume the edge. v3.0: Edge calculation uses calibrated probability from Confidence Calibration Engine, not raw agent confidence.
rules.enforcement: Orchestrator checks edge calculation (using calibrated probabilities and Kalshi settlement fees via Exchange Manager) before dispatching ExecutionOrder

rules.name: Liquidity Floor
rules.rule: Do not trade markets with less than $5,000 in 24-hour volume or where the orderbook spread exceeds 8%. Illiquid markets create slippage risk that destroys edge.
rules.enforcement: Market Scanner Tier 1 progressive loading filters out illiquid markets before they reach the Parliament

rules.name: Daily Loss Limit
rules.rule: If cumulative daily losses exceed 10% of starting-day bankroll, halt all trading for the remainder of the day. No exceptions. Resume at midnight UTC.
rules.enforcement: Portfolio Tracker monitors intraday P&L in USD; Execution Engine implements hard halt via Exchange Manager

rules.name: Consensus Requirement
rules.rule: Minimum 4 out of 6 agents must agree on direction before any trade is executed. This threshold CANNOT be lowered. 3:3 splits or worse result in NO_TRADE. EXCEPTION: Verified paired-contract arbitrage (YES + NO < 98 cents after Kalshi settlement fees on the same market) may bypass consensus requirement because the edge is mathematically defined, not probabilistic. Arbitrage bypass requires: (1) spread exceeds 2% after all fees, (2) both sides have sufficient liquidity for simultaneous execution, (3) Market Scanner and arb-detector both independently confirm the opportunity.
rules.enforcement: Orchestrator consensus logic — hardcoded, not configurable. Arbitrage carve-out enforced via separate code path with independent validation (see arb-detector skill).

rules.name: Dissent Acknowledgment
rules.rule: When a trade executes on a split vote (4:2 or 5:1), the dissent report MUST be logged and the position size MUST be reduced by at least 25% from Kelly-optimal. Unanimous (6:0) trades get full Kelly-fraction sizing.
rules.enforcement: Orchestrator applies automatic size reduction on split consensus; Kelly Sizer accepts consensus_split parameter

rules.name: Maximum Concurrent Positions
rules.rule: No more than 10 concurrent open positions at any time. Portfolio concentration beyond this level creates correlated risk that consensus cannot mitigate.
rules.enforcement: Portfolio Tracker blocks new ExecutionOrders when limit reached

rules.name: Time-to-Resolution Minimum
rules.rule: Do not enter markets resolving in less than 2 hours unless executing a paired-contract arbitrage (which is time-insensitive). Short-resolution markets have high volatility and limited time for edge to materialize.
rules.enforcement: Market Scanner Tier 1 progressive loading filters on resolution deadline (Kalshi market close_time via Exchange Manager)

rules.name: Kelly Fraction Cap
rules.rule: Use half-Kelly (0.5x Kelly-optimal) as the default position sizing. Full Kelly is too aggressive for prediction markets given model uncertainty. Quarter-Kelly (0.25x) for markets with high agent disagreement (4:2 split). v3.0: Kelly calculation uses calibrated probabilities, not raw confidence.
rules.enforcement: Kelly Sizer skill applies fraction based on consensus strength and calibrated confidence

rules.name: No Override Without Human Approval
rules.rule: No agent, orchestrator component, swarm validator, or automated process may disable or modify these rules. Only a human operator with direct CLAUDE.md file access can change risk parameters. The system must treat CLAUDE.md as immutable at runtime.
rules.enforcement: CLAUDE.md must be set to read-only permissions at OS level (chmod 444 / attrib +R) during trading sessions. Portfolio Tracker must perform a SHA-256 hash check of CLAUDE.md at startup and compare against a committed known-good hash; halt trading if mismatch detected. Changes require git commit and manual restart.

rules.name: Swarm Threshold
rules.rule: v3.0: Positions exceeding 3% of total bankroll must be validated by the Multi-Model Swarm before execution. Swarm refusal = NO_TRADE regardless of parliament consensus. Swarm reduce = position size cut by 50%. Swarm validation is optional for positions below this threshold.
rules.enforcement: Orchestrator checks position size against swarm_threshold before dispatching to Execution Engine; triggers swarm validator when threshold exceeded

rules.name: RBI Gate
rules.rule: v3.0: No new strategy type may be deployed live without first passing RBI Backtest Engine validation: minimum 100 simulated trades on Kalshi historical data, positive Sharpe ratio, and walk-forward validation on out-of-sample period. This applies to new agent configurations, new market categories, and new sizing rules.
rules.enforcement: Orchestrator checks strategy validation status before allowing trades in new categories or with new configurations. RBI Backtest Engine maintains a registry of validated strategies.

rules.name: Swarm Cost Budget
rules.rule: v3.0: Daily API spend on Multi-Model Swarm queries must not exceed $50 USD. When budget is exhausted, swarm validation is skipped for the remainder of the day and positions above swarm_threshold are capped at half their computed size as a compensating control.
rules.enforcement: Model Registry tracks cumulative daily spend; Orchestrator checks budget before triggering swarm

subagent_orchestration.description: How Claude Code's native subagent system is used to run the 6 specialist agents in parallel, with optional escalation to multi-model swarm.
subagent_orchestration.pattern: The Orchestrator is implemented as the primary Claude Code session. For each parliament vote, it spawns 6 subagents using Claude Code's built-in agent dispatch mechanism. Each subagent receives: (1) its specialist system prompt, (2) the CandidateMarket JSON with Kalshi market details (all prices in cents), (3) its domain-specific data feeds (pre-fetched by Market Scanner), and (4) access only to MCP tools relevant to its domain (e.g., Crypto Agent gets crypto market data tools but not economic data tools; Economics Agent gets FRED/BLS tools but not sports feeds). Subagents run in parallel with a 30-second timeout. Results are collected as structured JSON. v3.0: For high-value positions, a second round dispatches the trade question to 5+ external model providers via the Multi-Model Swarm Validator, running in parallel with a 45-second timeout. Claude Code hooks trigger Telegram alerts on dissent escalations, swarm refusals, calibration warnings, and circuit breaker activations.

agent_dispatch_config.retry_policy: No retries — timeout means the agent could not form a view in time, which is informative
agent_dispatch_config.isolation: Each subagent has its own system prompt, its own tool permissions, and its own data context. No shared state between agents during a voting session. Claude Code implementation: each subagent gets a different CLAUDE.md configuration scoping its data access — this is the mechanism for isolated context scoping.

result_schema.sources: string[], at least 1 source required unless ABSTAIN
result_schema.domain_signals: object, agent-specific structured data supporting the vote
result_schema.processing_time_ms: integer, how long the agent took to analyze
result_schema.data_freshness: object, timestamps of data feeds used — agent must report if primary data was unavailable

swarm_dispatch_config.timeout_behavior: Model excluded from consensus (does not count as vote)
swarm_dispatch_config.cost_tracking: Per-query cost tracked by Model Registry; cumulative daily spend checked against RISK-013 budget

progressive_signal_loading.description: Mechanism for incrementally adding or removing agents and data feeds without rebuilding the system, combined with tiered execution that optimizes for speed and computational efficiency. The Parliament is designed as a plug-in architecture where new specialist agents can be registered, existing agents can have their data feeds updated, and the consensus threshold adjusts automatically. Progressive context loading ensures basic checks run first, with deep computations firing only when warranted.
mechanism: TIER 1 (Basic Checks): Liquidity validation, spread check, contract availability, time-to-resolution filter. Run by Market Scanner on all scanned markets. Rejects 90%+ of scans with minimal computation. Target: <100ms per market.

TIER 2 (Edge Estimation): Implied probability calculation, P(real) vs P(market) comparison, EV computation, settlement fee impact. Run by market-analyzer skill on markets passing Tier 1. Target: <500ms per market.

TIER 3 (Parliament Dispatch): Full 6-agent parallel evaluation with isolated contexts, dissent processing, calibrated confidence aggregation. Run by parliament-session skill on markets passing Tier 2. Target: <120s per market.
TIER 4 (Swarm Validation): Multi-model cross-architecture validation. Triggered only for positions above swarm_threshold. Run by swarm-validator skill. Target: <60s additional latency.

Agent Registry: a JSON config file listing all active agents with their system prompts, tool permissions, data feed configurations, and Kalshi category assignments. Adding a new agent = adding an entry to this registry.
Dynamic Consensus Threshold: threshold is defined as ceil(n_agents * 0.6), so 4/6, 4/7, 5/8, etc. This maintains the ~60% supermajority requirement as agents are added.
Data Feed Routing: each agent's data feeds are defined in its registry entry. The Orchestrator's data loading step reads these configs and prepares isolated data packages dynamically.

Kalshi Category/Tag Mapping: each agent declares which Kalshi event categories and tags it specializes in (discoverable via GET /search/tags_by_categories through Exchange Manager). When new categories or tags appear on Kalshi, they can be assigned to existing agents or trigger creation of a new specialist. The Sports Agent additionally uses GET /search/filters_by_sport for sport-specific competition discovery.
Hot-swap Capability: agents can be disabled (set active: false) without removing them, allowing A/B testing of parliament configurations.

Signal Priority Levels: data feeds can be tagged as 'critical' (must load before vote), 'supplementary' (load if available, proceed without), or 'background' (async, may arrive after vote starts). This prevents slow data feeds from blocking the entire parliament.

Also define an agent_registry_schema for the Agent Registry config file, specifying required fields (agent_id, system_prompt, tool_permissions[], data_feed_configs[], kalshi_categories[], kalshi_tags[], subaccount_id?, active: boolean, model_provider?: string) so the Orchestrator can validate registry entries and route domain-specific data correctly. risks.description: All 6 parliament agents use the same underlying LLM (Claude), creating correlated failure modes. If the base model has a systematic bias or blind spot, all agents may share it despite having different prompts and data. v3.0 note: this is the primary motivation for the Multi-Model Swarm tier.
risks.mitigation: v3.0 mitigation: The Multi-Model Swarm Validator queries Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Llama on high-value trades, introducing genuine model architecture diversity. If all Claude parliament agents agree but non-Claude swarm models disagree, this signals a Claude-specific bias that the parliament alone cannot detect. For lower-value trades where swarm is not triggered, monitor for correlated errors across parliament agents using the Audit Trail's per-agent accuracy tracking. Consider long-term migration to mixed-model parliament (e.g., 3 Claude, 1 GPT, 1 Gemini, 1 Llama) if swarm consistently reveals Claude-specific biases.

risks.description: Domain-specific data feeds may be stale, incomplete, or unavailable. If the Economics Agent receives no Fed minutes, its vote quality degrades but it may still vote with false confidence.
risks.mitigation: Each agent must report data freshness in its vote response (see result_schema.data_freshness). If primary data feeds are unavailable, agent should ABSTAIN rather than guess. Implement data feed health monitoring with Telegram alerts on feed failures. v3.0: The Confidence Calibration Engine will detect agents voting confidently with stale data — if calibration shows degraded accuracy when data_freshness is old, the agent's calibration curve adjusts downward automatically.

risks.description: Market conditions can change between parliament vote completion and order execution. A 60-second deliberation window may be too slow for fast-moving markets. Adding swarm validation (v3.0) increases total latency by up to 60 additional seconds. Kalshi's orderbook may have thin liquidity on certain contracts.
risks.mitigation: Slippage protection: Execution Engine rejects trades where best available price has moved >2% from analysis time. For arbitrage opportunities (paired YES/NO contracts), bypass parliament for speed per the RISK-005 arbitrage carve-out. Use Kalshi WebSocket (via Exchange Manager) for real-time orderbook monitoring during execution. v3.0: Swarm validation adds latency only for high-value positions (>3% of bankroll) where the cost of a wrong decision justifies the extra validation time. Progressive context loading ensures most markets are rejected at Tier 1/2 in <500ms.

risks.description: The 23% ROI improvement was measured over only 14 days and 47 markets. The Science Agent's 80% dissent accuracy is from a 5-sample pilot. These sample sizes are insufficient for statistical significance. The system may be overfitting to a specific market regime.
risks.mitigation: Run extended paper trading on Kalshi demo API (minimum 30 days, 200+ markets) before deploying real capital. Track performance across multiple Kalshi event categories and market regimes. Implement walk-forward validation via RBI Backtest Engine: train weights on historical data, validate on subsequent unseen period. v3.0: The RBI Backtest Engine gates all strategies through historical validation (minimum 100 simulated trades, positive Sharpe) before live deployment. The Confidence Calibration Engine provides Brier scores and confidence intervals, making overfitting detectable. Science Agent dissent accuracy must reach 30+ solo-dissent events before any automated escalation decisions.

risks.description: If agents learn to agree with each other (prompt drift, shared training data updates), the consensus mechanism loses its value. The parliament degenerates into a single-agent system with extra steps.
risks.mitigation: Monitor inter-agent agreement rate. If it exceeds 85% over a 7-day window, it indicates loss of diversity. Trigger system prompt review and data feed isolation audit. Consider introducing a mandatory 'devil's advocate' rotation. v3.0: The Agent Diversity success metric tracks full vote split distribution (6:0, 5:1, 4:2, no-consensus) and alerts if 6:0 rate exceeds 35%. The Multi-Model Swarm provides a cross-architecture diversity check that is immune to prompt drift within the Claude parliament.

risks.description: Dependency on multiple external APIs (Kalshi, news feeds, FRED, crypto data feeds, plus in v3.0: OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Together AI for swarm). Any API outage, rate limit, or breaking change can disable part or all of the system.
risks.mitigation: Implement graceful degradation: if non-critical MCP servers are down, remaining agents still vote with available data. If Kalshi API is down, queue approved trades for execution when connectivity restores. v3.0: Exchange Manager provides centralized health checking and circuit breaking for Kalshi API. Model Registry provides health verification for swarm providers with fallback chains. If swarm providers are unavailable, swarm validation is skipped and position size is capped as compensating control per RISK-013. RSA-PSS signing is stateless (no token expiry risk). Cache market data to reduce API call frequency.

risks.description: Kalshi is a CFTC-regulated Designated Contract Market (DCM), which provides legal clarity for US-based trading. However, automated bot trading on regulated exchanges may still carry compliance considerations. CFTC regulations on event contracts could change.
risks.mitigation: Kalshi's CFTC regulation provides a significantly more favorable legal posture than offshore platforms. Maintain full audit trail for regulatory compliance. Operate within Kalshi's Terms of Service. Monitor CFTC regulatory developments via the Geopolitics Agent's data feeds. Implement a platform-specific kill switch via Exchange Manager that can disable all trading immediately. Legal review is still recommended before deployment to confirm automated trading permissibility on Kalshi. v3.0: Dissent reports include Kalshi-specific regulatory risk flags. Exchange Manager enforces jurisdictional routing (US = Kalshi only).

risks.description: Kalshi enforces per-market position limits (varies by contract, often $25K-$100K notional). The system must respect these limits, which may constrain position sizing on high-conviction trades.
risks.mitigation: Portfolio Tracker queries Kalshi market rules via Exchange Manager and enforces per-market position limits before order placement. Kelly Sizer output is capped at the lesser of CLAUDE.md max and Kalshi's per-market limit. For high-conviction trades near position limits, consider spreading across related markets within the same Kalshi event.

risks.description: v3.0: The Confidence Calibration Engine requires historical outcome data to build meaningful calibration curves. During the cold-start phase (first 50 settled votes per agent), calibration uses uninformative priors, meaning Kelly sizing operates on uncalibrated confidence. This period has the highest risk of position mis-sizing.
risks.mitigation: Use quarter-Kelly (0.25x) during the cold-start phase until each agent has 50+ settled votes with outcomes. Monitor Brier scores continuously — any agent with Brier score > 0.3 during cold-start should have its vote weight reduced. Run cold-start phase on Kalshi demo API with paper trading to accumulate calibration data before risking real capital.

risks.description: v3.0: Querying 5+ model providers per swarm validation incurs significant API costs. At $0.03-0.15 per query across providers, a busy day with 10 swarm validations could cost $1.50-7.50. Over time, this accumulates and may erode trading profits on smaller accounts.
risks.mitigation: RISK-013 enforces a daily swarm budget ($50/day). Model Registry tracks per-query costs. Swarm triggers only for positions above 3% of bankroll — small positions skip swarm entirely. Monitor swarm's incremental value: if swarm validation rarely changes parliament decisions, raise the threshold or reduce the minimum model count.

risks.description: v3.0: The source material (parliament 74% win rate, skill architecture $1K to $45K, PHANTOM $1.18 to $3.3M) consists of success stories that went viral. Identical architectures that failed are invisible. These results may not be reproducible, and no source provides confidence intervals, drawdown statistics during losing streaks, or performance across different market regimes.
risks.mitigation: Treat all source performance claims as directional hypotheses, not guaranteed outcomes. The RBI Backtest Engine provides the validation layer: no strategy goes live without backtesting on Kalshi historical data with confidence intervals. Track our own performance rigorously with Brier scores, calibration curves, and drawdown statistics. Define failure criteria upfront: if the system does not achieve 20% ROI over single-agent baseline within 90 days, conduct a full architecture review.

risks.description: v3.0: Multi-agent consensus assumes diversity of perspective creates robustness. But a truly novel event (unprecedented regulatory action, new Kalshi contract category, market regime never seen in training data) may produce uniform uncertainty across all agents AND all swarm models, making consensus meaningless.
risks.mitigation: The system's default behavior on uncertainty is NO_TRADE — when agents cannot reach consensus, no position is taken. This is the correct behavior for black swan events. Additionally, the daily loss limit (RISK-004) provides a hard cap on damage from any single regime. Monitor for correlated ABSTAIN votes across agents — if all 6 agents ABSTAIN on the same market, flag it as a potential blind spot for human review.

success_criteria.target: 20%+ improvement over single-agent approach on identical market set
success_criteria.measurement: A/B test: run parliament and single-agent on same Kalshi markets for 30 days, compare total ROI in USD

success_criteria.target: 74%+ on executed trades (vs ~60% single-agent baseline). A 'win' is defined as a settled or exited position where total USD return (payout minus cost minus Kalshi settlement fees) is strictly positive. Positions exited early at a loss count as losses. Positions exited early at a profit count as wins. Unsettled positions are excluded from win rate calculation until settled or exited.
success_criteria.measurement: Count of profitable settled/exited trades / total settled/exited trades executed by parliament

success_criteria.target: 50%+ reduction in average loss size compared to single-agent
success_criteria.measurement: Mean USD loss on losing trades: parliament vs single-agent baseline

success_criteria.target: Minority dissent accuracy > 60% when dissent quality score exceeds 70. Science Agent solo-dissent accuracy target: validate the 80% pilot figure over 30+ events before trusting for automated decisions.
success_criteria.measurement: Track outcomes of trades where high-quality dissent was overridden vs heeded. Separate tracking for Science Agent solo-dissent events.
success_criteria.timeframe: 60-day cumulative measurement (requires sufficient sample of 30+ dissent events)

success_criteria.target: < 15% of peak bankroll (in USD) at any point
System should refuse 40-60% of candidate markets (consensus not reached). Progressive loading should reject 90%+ at Tier 1/2 before reaching parliament.
success_criteria.measurement: Count of NO_TRADE decisions / total markets evaluated by parliament. Count of Tier 1/2 rejections / total markets scanned.

success_criteria.target: Full parliament vote cycle p50 < 60 seconds, p95 < 120 seconds from market dispatch to decision. Pre-fetched data packages must be delivered to agents at dispatch time. Swarm validation (when triggered) adds p50 < 30 seconds, p95 < 60 seconds additional.
success_criteria.measurement: Timestamp logging on Orchestrator: dispatch_time to decision_time, plus per-agent processing_time_ms breakdown and swarm_validation_time_ms
success_criteria.timeframe: Per-session, with p50, p95 and p99 tracking

success_criteria.target: Inter-agent unanimous agreement rate < 35% (agents should disagree frequently to demonstrate genuine analytical diversity). With 6 agents, track full vote split distribution: 6:0, 5:1, 4:2, and no-consensus outcomes. Healthy distribution target: 6:0 < 15%, 5:1 ~ 25-35%, 4:2 ~ 30-40%, no-consensus ~ 15-25%.
success_criteria.measurement: Percentage of parliament sessions by vote split pattern (6:0, 5:1, 4:2, no-consensus). Alert if 6:0 rate exceeds 35% over rolling window (indicates diversity collapse).

success_criteria.target: Per-agent Brier score < 0.25 after calibration (well-calibrated agents). No agent should have systematic bias exceeding 10% (e.g., claimed 80%, actual below 70% or above 90%) after the 50-vote cold-start phase.
success_criteria.measurement: Brier score per agent per Kalshi category. Calibration curve deviation from the diagonal. Computed by Confidence Calibration Engine.
success_criteria.timeframe: 30-day rolling, after 50+ settled votes per agent

success_criteria.target: Swarm validation should change parliament decisions on at least 10% but no more than 30% of triggered validations. Below 10% means swarm adds cost without value; above 30% means parliament is unreliable.
success_criteria.measurement: Count of swarm refusals + reductions / total swarm validations triggered

success_criteria.target: At least 60% of strategy hypotheses should be rejected by RBI backtesting before reaching live deployment. This validates that the gate is working — if everything passes, the bar is too low.
success_criteria.measurement: Count of rejected strategies / total strategies submitted to RBI Backtest Engine

notes:
v3.0 UPGRADE SUMMARY: This version integrates five major architectural concepts from the knowledge overview into the existing v2.0 parliament system:

1. PARLIAMENT WITH DISSENT REPORTS: Formalized the dissent mechanism as a first-class architectural component. The Science Agent's empirical role as 'most valuable minority dissenter' (4/5 correct on solo dissents, saving $890 — 5-sample pilot, validation pending) is systematically tracked and exploited via the Dissent Analyzer. Dissent reports now include Kalshi-specific regulatory risk flags. The key insight: 'A single dissenting agent proved more valuable than the rest of the system combined on its minority calls.'

2. MULTI-MODEL SWARM CONSENSUS: Added as an optional second tier on high-value positions. Queries Claude, GPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Llama in parallel to eliminate single-provider bias. The swarm does not replace the parliament — it ratifies or refuses parliament-approved trades. Different model architectures have different failure modes, so cross-model agreement provides a confidence signal that same-model parliament consensus cannot. The Model Registry enables easy model updates as new versions release.

3. SKILL ARCHITECTURE WITH PROGRESSIVE CONTEXT LOADING: Trading capabilities decomposed into modular skills (market-analyzer, kelly-sizer, bayesian-updater, dissent-reporter, parliament-session, arb-detector, swarm-validator) with typed I/O contracts. Progressive loading activates in 4 tiers: Tier 1 (basic checks, <100ms) -> Tier 2 (edge estimation, <500ms) -> Tier 3 (parliament, <120s) -> Tier 4 (swarm, <60s additional). Scans 147+ contracts per session but only 2-3 pass all tiers. This is the pattern that achieved 79% win rate and Sharpe 2.59 in the source material.

4. RBI FRAMEWORK: Research-Backtest-Implement gates all strategies through historical validation using Kalshi's archived market data (GET /historical/markets, GET /historical/trades) before live deployment. No strategy goes live without minimum 100 simulated trades, positive Sharpe, and walk-forward validation. This addresses the survivorship bias risk (R-011) head-on.

5. EXCHANGE MANAGER: A routing abstraction layer decoupling all trading logic from Kalshi-specific API details. Currently configured with Kalshi as the sole adapter (US-legal, CFTC-regulated). Enables future platform additions without changing agent logic. Enforces jurisdictional routing (US = Kalshi only for CFTC compliance).

NEW IN V3.0 — CONFIDENCE CALIBRATION: Addresses the knowledge gap identified in the overview where 'confidence calibration across agents is unaddressed.' The Confidence Calibration Engine maintains per-agent, per-domain calibration curves mapping raw confidence to calibrated probabilities. Uses Platt scaling or isotonic regression. Bootstraps with uninformative priors during cold-start (first 50 votes per agent), then switches to empirical calibration. Feeds calibrated probabilities to Kelly Sizer for more accurate position sizing.

NEW IN V3.0 — KNOWLEDGE GAPS ADDRESSED:
- Kalshi API orchestration: Exchange Manager provides the missing Kalshi adapter layer. All Kalshi-specific details (RSA-PSS signing, cents pricing, contract types, rate limits) are encapsulated in the Exchange Manager, with a platform-agnostic interface above.
- Confidence calibration: Confidence Calibration Engine with Brier scores, calibration curves, and systematic bias detection.
- Agent disagreement resolution: Dissent Analyzer with quality scoring, historical accuracy tracking, and graduated response (PROCEED/REDUCE_SIZE/HUMAN_REVIEW/ABORT). Automated handling gated behind 30-event minimum sample size per agent.
- Infrastructure costs: RISK-010 and RISK-013 address swarm API costs with daily budgets. Model Registry tracks per-query costs.
- Survivorship bias: RISK-011 explicitly acknowledges this risk. RBI Backtest Engine provides the validation gate.

OPEN-SOURCE REFERENCES: Four repos inform the implementation — Paperclip (general agent framework), MiroFish (prediction market bot), Hermes by Nous Research (parliament-style voting, most relevant for consensus mechanisms), and OpenClaw (Claude Code integration, most relevant for skill/subagent patterns). These are starting points, not production Kalshi integrations.

CLAUDE CODE INFRASTRUCTURE: The architecture maps naturally to Claude Code's native capabilities: MCP servers for Kalshi API and data feeds, CLAUDE.md for immutable risk rules loaded into every agent's context, Skills for encapsulating each trading capability (market-analyzer, kelly-sizer, etc.) as reusable modules with progressive loading, Subagents for running parliament members in parallel with isolated context scoping (each gets different system prompt + tool permissions), and Hooks for event-driven Telegram alerts on fills, dissent escalations, swarm refusals, calibration warnings, and circuit breaker activations.

KEY ARCHITECTURAL INSIGHT (unchanged from v2.0): The Parliament's edge comes NOT from any individual agent being smarter, but from the built-in mechanism of doubt that a single model cannot replicate. The most profitable traders 'almost never bet on the same thing at the same time' — they think differently, and that diversity is exactly what makes each profitable. The architecture replicates this cognitive diversity synthetically through isolated contexts and specialized data feeds. v3.0 adds a second layer of diversity through multi-model swarm consensus — not just different perspectives on the same model, but fundamentally different model architectures evaluating the same question.

CRITICAL ANTI-PATTERN (unchanged from v2.0): Giving all agents the same information. If every agent sees everything, they converge on the same conclusion, and the parliament becomes a single agent with 6x the cost and zero additional insight. Information isolation between agents is not a nice-to-have — it is the fundamental mechanism that creates the edge.
